independent.summary: Retrieval is now pinned to the sweep floor (0.60), but ragThreshold is valid down to 0.50 (Entity.js:65, entitySettings.js:111). For an entity set below 0.60 the pass is stricter than the entity's own threshold, so the "top page" column no longer reflects what that entity actually retrieves — a question with topScore 0.58 and threshold 0.55 prints hit ✅ (score >= threshold) yet '—' for the page, and the sweep table has no '← entity' row at all.

thresholdRange derives the step count with Math.round((max-min)/step), so a step that does not divide the range evenly emits candidates past max: thresholdRange(0.6, 0.8, 0.03) returns a final 0.81 and thresholdRange(0.6, 0.8, 0.07) likewise ends at 0.81, outside the requested bound. Unreached by the defaults, and the tests only cover divisible/degenerate steps.

triageGrades.reason: The change adds a pure scoring module, a CLI script edit and a unit test; no auth, role or session code is involved.
No credentials, tokens or env-var handling are added or changed (the script's existing MONGODB_URI use is untouched).
No billing, Stripe, quota or pricing code is touched; the only cost note is that the sweep adds no embedding calls.
Read-only: sweepThresholds is pure and the script only adds a retrieval pass and console output — no writes, deletes or migrations.
No new external call; retrieveContext is still invoked once per question, only with a different threshold argument.
No deploy, build, config or dependency changes — a new service file, a dev script and a test file only.

summary: The local model found nothing and its triage is entirely correct, but it also missed both (admittedly low-severity) edge cases — the sub-0.60 ragThreshold reporting inconsistency and thresholdRange overshooting max on a non-divisible step — so it offered no actual review signal on a change that is otherwise sound and faithful to the item.
